column1: # The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2): the base dump and update v131072 (1.1.1). Nintendo SDK 22.2.8, NVN2.

column2: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

column1: # v0 is the base dump the profile was brought up on; v131072 (1.1.1) is the update a NUP carries alone, the whole game. Their modules are the same builds, and the shader tables
# split from v131072 are v0's key for key: the tables are v131072's, so a NUP of the update packs from the profile as it is

# In the NUP at hand three RomFS files begin with 12 KB of zeros (the container's SHA-256 of them matches, so they were so when it was packed; whether a retail copy has them is not known), so they cannot be decompressed. Served as stored, the fairy
# fountain model that uses the first never loaded and the OptimizeChangeBanc thread (main+0xf7a0) asked for it again ~22 times a second all session: one core, plus ~0.75 core of
# ParallelDecompThread decompressing the 2.4 MB model each time (Mac CPU 365%, iPad 400-460%). "Not found" fails the model the same way. Served as the game's own 1x1 flat normal map, the
# model loads once and both threads go idle (Mac CPU 412% -> 180%, frame p95 21.9 -> 18.8 ms). The Ganon stage bake is served as its neighbour cell's (not checked in game). A copy without the damage
# needs none of this: the host substitutes only a .zs file that is not a zstd stream (hle_fs.c img_serve)
# The NPDM declares 48 MiB of system resources. Startup requests a 6.20 GiB heap.
# The alias region holds the game's streaming allocator (main+0x7ed630): in Kokiri Forest about 5,100 address regions with 3.0-3.3 GB mapped, reaching +4.95 GB (DM_REGIONS).

# On the Mac the region is 64 GB of address space whatever this key says (hle_svc.c, e9d71e27): mem_alias sizes the heap, mem_reserve - 256 MB - mem_alias - mem_stack = 0x248000000, which holds the 0x18ce00000 request, and an iPhone's region.

# The pool less the heap leaves 2.80 GiB for the alias region. The game's heap there (NinVirtualAddressHeap, main+0x7ed440) gives pages back at once and does not retry a refused map, and its free size is the OS's total - used (main+0x7ef010):
# with this key used counts the mapped pages, as on Horizon. Without it free never falls, whatever is mapped: 4.50 GB in our 49-minute run, 5.25 GB in #1445.
# agl wraps its depth clears in render conditions, as on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders: in Kokiri Forest the main opaque pass tests EQUAL against a copy of the prepass depth
# that a conditional clear (skipped on the console) wiped first, so no lit geometry landed and the full-screen sky showed through everywhere (a white scene)

# Off here, on in main's profile: unproven on this host. Tested, they do not fix the terrain (its height tiles have their own fix, nvn-objects.md, height tiles over storage the GPU wrote earlier), a 49-minute

# session into Hyrule Field ran without them, and with them on every registered texture's pages are write-protected and listed. Stale or black textures past Hyrule Field are the sign to try them: a host build, no shader rebuild
# The scene camera for MetalFX's motion vectors (DM_UPSCALER=metalfx-temporal, DM_MFX_INTERP; nvn_mfx.inc): gsys's Context uniform block at vertex uniform 0 of the scene passes, the view
# (3x4 rows) at +0x0 and the view-projection at +0x30, as on Donkey Kong Bananza. Read in a run (DM_MFX_PROBE, v131072): the opening's 3D cutscenes and Link's house give a GL perspective
# camera (50 degrees, 16:9, near 0.1, far 25037, no projection offset) in the 1920x1080 D32F depth pass that matches the upscaler's input; 15,000 upscaler frames, none without a camera
# Dynamic resolution reads the GPU time between two timestamp reports of the frame (main+0x5a8f0): with one time for the whole submission it is 0 and the rate never moves. At fixed 720p
# in Hyrule Field the frame time is the same (README.md, Render resolution)
# Metal encoding on its own thread: in Link's house at rate 3.0 it takes MetalFX's temporal scaler from 30.7 to 25.4 ms a frame (GPU p50 24.2 to 17.9), and the game's own upscaler stays at 18.7
# The resolution chain the host logs at launch (loader.c res_chain_log) and the launcher's render sizes (settings.py rate_base): the upscaler's output docked (the 2560x1440 window: ResolutionParam's
# FinalImageResolution, one resample), the same with single upscale (the game has no stub for it), handheld 1920x1080, the game's own rates (its palette's scales 0.75 to 0.333: 1.3333 to 3.0),
# and the rate a stage starts at (level 0: 1.3333; in a run docked 1920x1080 -> 2560x1440 from the stage's first frame)
